mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 3.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% month-over-month indicates weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market that amplifies wage inflation and input costs, compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production (INDPRO) expansion of more than 1% coupled with a concurrent decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% indicates a supply-side shock that boosts real output while suppressing inflation, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate to below 1% within a single month signals an emergency monetary easing that lowers risk-free rates and boosts present value of equities, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) above 0.5% for six consecutive months signals improving consumer purchasing power, which boosts demand and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% and a fall in average hourly earnings (not directly observed but implied by labor market slack) over two months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that depress corporate earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline of more than 5% in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a synchronized collapse in demand components, which reliably precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.
